data.description:
## Summary

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`'s `mcp_run_new` carries `-e FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*'`, but NO test
asserts it. Deleting that line leaves the whole suite green while every blue-green-deployed MCP
container stops trusting nginx's `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` — silently reinstating the
HTTPS->HTTP downgrade that fernlike-toothsome-hen (79b2-6ebc-6c1d-4125) fixed, on the only path
MCP actually ships through. The flag guards a P1 security fix and is itself unguarded.

Discovered while widening that ticket's file_impact: its plan claimed the compose-parity oracle
covered this var. It does not. `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` has exactly one parity
test, `test_autodeploy_mcp_run_new_passes_the_bedrock_region`, and it loops only over
`_MCP_REGION_VARS = ("REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION", "AWS_DEFAULT_REGION")` (line 763). There is no
`_ENV_FILE_ONLY` set in that file; the `.env` non-interpolation rationale lives separately in
`test_autodeploy_carries_the_jira_variables_by_env_file_not_by_dash_e` (line 639).

Compose IS covered — `test_compose_mcp_trusts_the_edge_forwarded_proto` asserts
`FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS == "*"` on the `mcp` service. Only the autodeploy `docker run` is unguarded,
and that is the path an actual deploy takes.

## Approach

Extend the existing parity coverage in `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`, reusing the
helper that is already there:

1. `_mcp_run_new_body()` (line ~788) already extracts just the `mcp_run_new` body, so a match in
   a sibling function cannot count. Reuse it — do not re-read the script.
2. Add a test asserting the body contains the flag, mirroring the region test's substring form
   (`-e {var}=` or `-e "{var}=`), and additionally that the VALUE is the literal `*`, since a
   pinned bridge-gateway address is exactly the drift the compose test already rejects.
3. Keep it a separate named test rather than folding `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS` into
   `_MCP_REGION_VARS` — that tuple is documented as the Bedrock region pair and is asserted
   against compose's region-agreement invariant, which does not apply to this var.

The mutation check that proves the test works: delete the `-e FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*'` line from
`mcp_run_new` and confirm the new test goes RED (today nothing does), then restore it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test in `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` fails when `mcp_run_new`'s body does not
      pass `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`. Verified by deleting the `-e FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*'` line
      from `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` and observing that test go RED, then restoring it.
- [ ] That test also fails when the value is present but not the literal `*` (e.g. a pinned
      gateway address such as `172.17.0.1`). Verified by substituting that value and observing
      RED, then restoring.
- [ ] The test scopes its match to `mcp_run_new` only, via the existing `_mcp_run_new_body()`
      helper, so an occurrence in a sibling shell function cannot satisfy it. Verified by
      reading the test body.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` passes on unmodified `main`.

## Testing

Pure structural test over committed text — the same tier as the surrounding tests in that file.
No nginx binary, no docker, no network.

## File impact

`tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` (test-only; no source change — the flag it guards is
already committed and deployed).

## Compat / rollback

Additive: one new test function. No production code changes. Rollback is deleting the test.

## Portability

Runs under plain `pytest` by parsing a committed file. No CI provider is involved and no deploy
host is contacted, so it holds anywhere the repo is checked out.
data.title: Guard the autodeploy FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS flag with a compose-parity test
